studies.Authors: Rebbeck TR, Troxel AB, Norman S, Bunin GR, DeMichele A, Baumgarten M, Berlin M, Schinnar R, Strom BL
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Use of HRS was associated with breast cancer risk, using a population-based case-control study... Use of black cohosh had a significant breast cancer protective effect

extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: Use of black cohosh had a significant breast cancer protective effect (adjusted odds ratio 0.39, 95% CI: 0.22-0.70)
extraction_supporting_text.p_value: Computed from the reported effect and 95% CI using a normal approximation: p=0.001.

studies.Reference: The use of herbal preparations to alleviate climacteric disorders and risk of postmenopausal breast cancer in a German case-control study.

studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Information on HEP use was collected in face-to-face interviews supported by a list of brand names.

extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: Ever use of HEP (9.9%) was inversely associated with invasive breast cancer [odds ratio (OR), 0.74; 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.63-0.87]
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: inversely associated with invasive breast cancer
extraction_supporting_text.p_value: dose-dependent manner (OR, 0.96 per year of use; P = 0.03)
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: herbal preparations (HEP) containing phytoestrogens and black cohosh

headline.funnel_interpretation: Insufficient studies to perform formal publication bias testing.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 2 studies yielded an effect size of 0.61 (95% CI: 0.34–1.07), indicating no statistically significant association between black cohosh and breast cancer. Although the point estimate suggests a potential inverse relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by very high heterogeneity (I² = 76.38%), reflecting highly inconsistent results across studies.
